description: We are a team of 6 students from Salalah, Oman, studying at the University of Technology and Applied Sciences (UTAS). We are passionate about technology, innovation, and solving real-world problems. Our project is an early fire detection website designed to help detect fires quickly, provide real-time alerts, and support faster emergency response.
summary: Cinderscope is a web app that turns NASA's MODIS and VIIRS active-fire detections into one consistent, comparable record. The two sensors see fire differently (1 km vs 375 m pixels), so their raw counts cannot be compared or joined. Cinderscope maps every NASA FIRMS detection onto a common equal-area 5 km grid per UTC day, labels each cell as MODIS-only, VIIRS-only or shared, and measures agreement. Users explore an interactive map and calendar, trace every cell back to the original NASA records, ask a rule-based investigator that answers only from the data, and export reports with full provenance. Using the FIRMS archive for Zimbabwe, it builds a harmonized 2003–2025 record by scaling MODIS to the VIIRS level, validated on held-out years (daily error reduced by 36%). It works offline and states its limits openly: detections are not confirmed fires, and cloud coverage is unknown.
details:
WHAT IT DOES: Cinderscope compares NASA MODIS and VIIRS fire hotspots on one common grid. It cleans FIRMS CSV files, removes exact duplicates, keeps nominal and high confidence detections, and assigns each detection to an equal-area 5 km cell for its UTC day. Each cell-day is MODIS-only, VIIRS-only or shared, and agreement is shared ÷ all occupied cells.

FEATURES: Interactive map with calendar playback; sensor filters (MODIS / VIIRS / Shared); evidence panel linking every cell to original NASA records; a rule-based investigator that answers only from the data and never guesses fire causes; a 2003–2025 harmonized record for Zimbabwe; JSON/CSV export with checksums and coverage limits; offline use and installation as an app.

HARMONIZED RECORD: A monthly VIIRS÷MODIS factor learned from 2012–2025 scales older MODIS years to the VIIRS level. Tested on held-out years: 2025 daily error fell from 72.5 to 46.5 cells/day (−36%); median yearly-total error 5.7%.

IMPACT: Gives researchers and fire managers a longer, consistent fire-activity record and makes sensor disagreement visible instead of hidden.

TOOLS: TypeScript, Vite, Leaflet, Vitest, Playwright, Node.js. AI coding assistance (Claude) was used to write code, tests and documentation, reviewed by the team.

LIMITS: Detections are not confirmed fires; cloud/overpass coverage is unknown; the sensor ratio drifts over time, so older years carry uncertainty ranges.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS Active Fire Data (MODIS C6.1 & VIIRS C2)
